"Kings go in the corners. Play your cards solitaire fashion and extend your turn as long as you can. Can't make a single play? Pay the pot. First to empty your hand? You win the pot...plus your opponents' point chips for their unplayed cards! Reach 100 points? You win the game."
—description from the publisher

Each round, the players shuffle a regular card deck (included), deal out hands of 7 cards and divide up 80 chips among themselves. The shared central playing field is seeded with 4 cards. In turns, each player places cards from their hand into the central field using typical solitaire rules of alternating suit colors and strictly sequential cards in declining value order. Any kings cards in the initial deal or drawn later are placed in the "corner" slots at the player's first opportunity. Solitaire card chains are placed in descending order on the kings.

In the retail version the central playing field is a plastic hub which has four "king" slots and four "tabbed" slots for the available places to build the chains of cards.

"After one player wins the hand by being the first to get rid of all his/her cards, the other players put one chip in the pot for each of the cards remaining in their hand. The winner of the hand receives all the chips in the pot and records the number of chips for his/her score. Each chip is worth one point. All the chips are then collected to be redistributed for the next hand to be played. The first player to accumulate 100 points is the winner of the game."
—description from the publisher

The game length can vary quite a bit to get to 100 points for one player.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Almost pure luck, with no strategy, but made worse because you have to pay close attention to make sure you don't miss making the right move.

[Rating: 1/10] I'd question whether this can be called a game but there are possibly moments in a 2+ player game where a decision might matter.

[Rating: 2/10] $1 at a used book sale... my wife made me buy it :-).  I'm hoping to get rid of it.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't HATE it...but it's pretty boring.  UPDATE: OK - now I officially *do* hate it.  Dropped from a 4.

[Rating: 2/10] An atrocious game that takes too long (it would be more fun if it was a speed game), has components that both don't work and damage the cards and worst of all just isn't fun.

[Rating: 2/10] Simple card game my babysitter taught me when I was young. Don't think I will ever play this again.

[Rating: 2/10] Maybe I just don't get this game, but it seems to be entirely luck based with the only skill or decision or whatever happening maybe once or twice per game to not miss the really important move you need to make to not be out of the running entirely. Not fun to play either.

[Rating: 3/10] --Jul2007-- Played this with my parents, at their suggestion.  Sad to say, I really wasn't amused.  I suppose it's a game, of sorts, but I perceived no interesting decisions to be made.  It could be, of course, that I lack the fine perceptions necessary.
